ing: 5 oz each, drained, or smoked tuna
st: If using dry shredded coconut, sprinkle it with [[2 tbsp]] warm water and let it soften for 10 minutes.
Flake the drained tuna into a bowl with a fork.
Add the coconut, onion, chili, curry leaves and salt.
Squeeze in the lime juice.
Mix with your fingers, pressing and rubbing so the flavors blend and the mixture is moist and crumbly.
Taste and add more chili, lime or salt as you like.
Serve at once with warm roshi or flatbread and hot tea.
Bring the water to a boil in a medium pot.
Add the onion, chilies, curry leaves, salt and pepper and boil for 5 minutes.
Add the tuna chunks and reduce the heat to a gentle simmer.
Cook for 12 minutes until the fish is firm and the broth is clear. Skim off any foam.
Remove the fish and flake it into large pieces, or leave it in chunks.
Return the fish to the broth and add the lime juice. Taste and adjust the salt.
Serve the broth hot in bowls with rice and lime wedges on the side.
Toss the tuna with half of the salt and half of the lime juice. Rest for 10 minutes.
Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat and cook the onion for 5 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger, chilies, curry leaves and curry powder, stirring for 2 minutes.
Pour in the coconut milk and water and bring to a low simmer.
Add the tuna and remaining salt.
Simmer gently for 12 minutes, without stirring much, until the tuna is cooked through and the sauce thickens.
Stir in the remaining lime juice. Serve with rice or roshi.
Mix the flour, salt and grated coconut in a bowl.
Stir in [[1 tbsp]] of the oil, then add the warm water a little at a time to form a soft dough.
Knead for 5 minutes until smooth. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Divide the dough into 8 equal balls.
On a floured surface, roll each ball into a very thin circle about 7 inches wide.
Heat a dry skillet or flat griddle over medium-high heat.
Cook each roshi for 1 to 2 minutes per side until brown spots appear, brushing lightly with the remaining oil.
Stack the roshi in a clean towel to stay soft. Serve warm with curry or mas huni.
Mix the flour, [[0.5 tsp]] of the salt and the coconut oil. Add the warm water to form a soft dough. Knead for 5 minutes, cover, and rest for 30 minutes.
For the filling, mix the tuna, coconut, onion, chili, lime juice, curry leaves and remaining salt.
Divide the dough into 18 pieces and roll each into a ball.
Flatten a ball in your palm and put about [[1 tbsp]] filling in the middle.
Pull the dough up around the filling, pinch to close, and roll into a smooth ball.
Heat the oil to 350°F (175°C).
Fry in batches for 4 minutes, turning, until deep golden brown.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a pan over medium heat and cook the onion for 4 minutes. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the cabbage, curry powder, salt and pepper and cook for 5 minutes until the cabbage is soft and dry.
Mix in the tuna and let the filling cool for 15 minutes.
Fold in the chopped eggs.
Mix the flour with [[1 tbsp]] water to make a paste.
Place about [[3 tbsp]] filling on a wrapper, fold the sides in, roll up tightly, and seal the edge with the paste.
Heat the oil to 350°F (175°C) in a deep pan.
Fry in batches for 3 minutes, turning, until golden and crisp. Drain and serve hot.
Mix the chili powder, garlic, ginger, turmeric, salt, curry leaves, lime juice and oil into a paste.
Make 3 or 4 slashes in each side of the fish.
Rub the paste into the slashes and all over the fish.
Marinate in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.
Heat a grill or broiler to high. Oil the grate.
Grill for 5 to 6 minutes per side, until the fish flakes and reaches 145°F (63°C).
Serve with lime wedges, rice or roshi.
Put the rice and water in a heavy pot and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer on low for 20 minutes until the water is mostly absorbed and the rice is soft.
Stir in the coconut milk, sugar, cardamom and salt.
Cook over low heat for 20 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy.
Mash a few grains of rice against the pot to thicken it more, if you like.
Taste and add sugar if needed.
Serve warm or chilled, sprinkled with cashews. It will thicken as it cools.
